items.title: William Russell Interview, 1976-02-16
items.q: I always remember Leonard Feather talking about who didn't like Bunk at all...

ctx.x: I mean, look at, well, 1940, I was thinking about Louis and Bechet getting together in that band. Bro on bass, you know, where they made the Colcord Blues and done it. Wanky Dock Town and all those things.

By the way, when they, they had an Esquire program, they had an all-star band, you know, Esquire. And so they gave some of the awards down here. I think it was a three-way hookup they had. Benny Goodman was in New York, somebody in San Francisco, and Louis, I believe, in New Orleans. The three of them or so got together. Well, anyway, they played one piece over earphones. But they also gave a concert here at the auditorium. They had George Lewis's band. Bunk was there, too. Is that the night they changed the…
And tell him you've only got about two or three minutes. Yeah.

items.title: William Russell Interview, 1976-02-16
items.q: Go Fan had written the book.

ctx.x: Of course there hadn't been written, hadn't been any full length book written on the subject of jazz.

Well, yeah. Go Fan had written the book. And also Panassier's book came out I think in this country about 1936. Maybe even 35, I'd have to look up the date. But there's no other American books at least had been written. I think Hobson's was about the first one really. A full length book of Wilder Hobson. And that was more like 1938 I guess.

Well, Jazzmen is known outside of, well in academic circles where I'm from as the first definitive book on American jazz. That is from the point of view of the musicians. Yeah, well it wasn't exactly definitive.
